  Destination: NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL PCR Full Skirt (slot 3). Reading of the request: 6
    samples x 3.

Labware for the technique (qPCR setup): nothing to flag.

  slot labware                               well  liquid                       load at least  declared
  2    Opentrons 24 Tube Rack with NEST 2 mL A1    master mix                           144.0     200.0
  4    Opentrons 96 Well Aluminum Block with A1    sample 1                               6.0      10.0

protocol.py: 6 biology problems (2 errors, 1 warning, 3 notes).

1. ERROR CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: master mix (tube A1 in slot 2)
   line 61:  p20.aspirate(8, tube_rack["A1"])
   At line 61 the tip went into master mix (tube A1 in slot 2) while it still carried sample
   1 (well A1 in slot 4), sample 2 (well A2 in slot 4), sample 3 (well A3 in slot 4), sample
   4 (well A4 in slot 4) and 2 more from an earlier step (this line did it 6 times). A tip
   that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this
   stock now holds material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from it then took the
   unwanted material along into 15 other wells: wells A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9, A10, A11 and 7
   more in slot 3.
   Affected: tube A1 in slot 2.
   Also reached 15 other wells: wells A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9, A10, A11 and 7 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 61 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [47cbcce8d1d2]

2. ERROR CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: 6 stocks
   line 69:  p20.aspirate(2, sample_source)
   At line 69 the tip went into sample 1 (well A1 in slot 4), sample 2 (well A2 in slot 4),
   sample 3 (well A3 in slot 4), sample 4 (well A4 in slot 4) and 2 more while it still
   carried master mix (tube A1 in slot 2), sample 1 (well A1 in slot 4), sample 2 (well A2
   in slot 4), sample 3 (well A3 in slot 4) and 2 more from an earlier step (this line did
   it 6 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid
   it touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn
   from them then took the unwanted material along into 14 other wells: wells A5, A6, A7,
   A8, A9, A10, A11, A12 and 6 more in slot 3.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and A6 in slot 4.
   Also reached 14 other wells: wells A5, A6, A7, A8, A9, A10, A11, A12 and 6 more in slot
   3.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 69 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [33e1f455bdcc]

3. WARNING COLD-MODULE-NEVER-SET: A temperature module was loaded but never set
   line 69:  p20.aspirate(2, sample_source)
   At line 69 the robot draws from wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and A6 in slot 4, on a
   temperature module that the protocol never sets. A temperature module stays at room
   temperature until `set_temperature` is called, so sample 1 (sample), sample 2 (sample),
   sample 3 (sample), sample 4 (sample) and 2 more sat on a block that was never cold; the
   robot pipetted there 18 times over the run. The person setting up the deck sees a module
   and assumes it is cold. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and A6 in slot 4.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and A6 in slot 4.
   Fix: Call `temp_module.set_temperature(4)` before the first transfer from Opentrons 96
   Well Aluminum Block with Generic PCR Strip 200 µL in slot 4, and
   `temp_module.deactivate()` at the end.
   Source: Opentrons, temperature module: at room temperature until set_temperature, which
   blocks
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/temperature_module.html
   Source: Thermo Fisher T4 ligase manual: keep on ice, use within minutes
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/t4dnaligase_1U_man.pdf
   Source: NEB: Q5 High-Fidelity PCR kit manual (add the polymerase last)
           https://www.neb.com/-/media/nebus/files/manuals/manuale0555.pdf
   [cb33f0e026fe]

4. NOTE NO-SAMPLE-INTO-REAGENT-WELL: (proposed) A tip that had been in a sample went into a
reagent
   line 61:  p20.aspirate(8, tube_rack["A1"])
   At line 61 the tip touched the liquid in tube A1 in slot 2 while it still carried sample
   1 (well A1 in slot 4), sample 2 (well A2 in slot 4), sample 3 (well A3 in slot 4), sample
   4 (well A4 in slot 4) and 2 more from an earlier step (this line did it 6 times). A tip
   that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, and the
   protocol never transfers that liquid into this well on purpose. A reagent is shared: the
   master mix, the enzyme or the primer in that well goes into every reaction on the plate.
   A tip that has been in one sample leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so
   a sample carried into a reagent well turns up in every well that reagent reaches, and a
   no-template control can no longer be trusted. Liquid was later taken out of the affected
   wells, and the unwanted material went along into 15 other wells: wells A4, A5, A6, A7,
   A8, A9, A10, A11 and 7 more in slot 3.
   Affected: tube A1 in slot 2.
   Also reached 15 other wells: wells A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9, A10, A11 and 7 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Use a fresh tip for each sample at line 61, or add the reagent to the wells first,
   while the tip is clean, and the samples afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [eb3b52fdd65e]

5. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No no-template control: 18 wells of master mix with a sample
   line 63:  p20.dispense(8, plate[well])
   At line 63 the robot starts putting master mix into NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL PCR Full
   Skirt (slot 3), and 18 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate
   holds the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is
   contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing
   on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8
   and 10 more in slot 3.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 10 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 8 ul of master mix and 2 ul of water in place of
   the template, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [86e0697076ac]

6. NOTE UNMIXED-AT-END: 18 wells never mixed after sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4
and 2 more went in (20% of the well)
   line 71:  p20.dispense(2, plate[well])
   At line 71 the robot added sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 2 more to wells A1,
   A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 10 more in slot 3, which already held master mix (this
   line did it 18 times). The addition was 20% of the well, nothing mixed the well
   afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do
   not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated.
   A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one will not be,
   mix it.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 10 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 10 more in slot 3 after line 71:
   `mix_after=(5, 8)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 8, well)`, with the volume about
   80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [6ee3f8ac7247]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.

findings.title: A used tip went into a stock: master mix (tube A1 in slot 2)
findings.explanation: At line 61 the tip went into master mix (tube A1 in slot 2) while it still carried sample 1 (well A1 in slot 4), sample 2 (well A2 in slot 4), sample 3 (well A3 in slot 4), sample 4 (well A4 in slot 4) and 2 more from an earlier step (this line did it 6 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from it then took the unwanted material along into 15 other wells: wells A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9, A10, A11 and 7 more in slot 3.
